title: Additive contract generations and adoption boundary
summary: Accounting Core evolves through additive contracts so existing company adapters can adopt newer tax/reporting/lifecycle layers incrementally. The event/transaction/posting path remains the accounting spine; persistence, scopes, tax, settlement and reporting evidence are layered above or beside it.
invariants: accounting.event/0.1 and accounting.transaction/0.1 are the preferred operational integration spine.
accounting.store/0.1 makes the same legal-entity book restartable without changing authority semantics.
accounting.tax/0.1 and accounting.settlement/0.1 produce evidence-bound determinations that enter ordinary accounting policy rather than posting directly.
accounting.reporting/0.1 selects live views; accounting.reporting.snapshot/0.1 seals exact populations; attestation/submission and filing/lifecycle contracts sit above that evidence.
A consumer should adopt only the layers it needs; newer reporting features must not force an operational engine to change its existing accounting-event contract.
A sphere or documentation statement never supersedes a newer executable Accounting Core artifact in the same workspace.

provenance.claim: v0.10 is additive over earlier accounting contract generations and preserves existing consumer APIs.
v0.10 retains all earlier transaction, persistence, tax, settlement, scope/reporting and assessment qualifications.
